title: Humane rollback controller for private data-plane updates
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Problem: Private (VPC) customers require zero-downtime runtime rollouts for data-plane upgrades, but current automation lacks a clear, safe rollback path when KV cache priming, short-lived sessions, or tenant-specific warmup characteristics cause degraded tail-latency or correctness regressions. This ticket designs and implements a humane rollback controller that minimizes blast radius and operator toil by combining tenant-aware phased swaps, synthetic health assertions, progressive backout, and Terraform-controlled orchestration.
goals: 1) Provide deterministic, auditable rollback decisions for private runtime upgrades. 2) Ensure no more than 5% of active tenant sessions see >150ms p99 regression during a rollout. 3) Automate fast rollback within 90s of detection while preserving client connections where possible. 4) Surface clear signals to operators via Console and Slack alerts.
success_metrics:
- Rollback-triggered by automated controller reduces incident escalations by 60% in staging runs.
- Median rollback time under 90s after threshold breach.
- <1% of tenants experience error-rate increase >0.5% in canary phase across 5 test runs.
proposed_design:
High-level components:
- Rollout Orchestrator (controller) that speaks to IaC layer (Terraform state via orchestration API) and the runtime control plane.
- Tenant Awareness: controller partitions tenant set into slices based on traffic shape and session persistence.
- Synthetic Health Assertions: deploy synthetic prober pods per slice to exercise primed KV paths, long-prompt token streams, and cold-start scenarios.
- Decision Engine: small finite-state-machine that consumes latency/error thresholds, probe results, and third-party metrics (trace-derived tail-latency) to decide continue/hold/rollback.
- Graceful Backout: controller attempts connection-preserving rollback where runtime supports session handoff; otherwise performs a staged traffic drain with rapid reattachment to previous model variant.
- IaC hooks: Terraform module will expose plan time metadata and an operator API that allows controller to advance or revert a change via pre-signed apply/run steps.
rollout_plan:
1) Stage: add controller to private staging clusters; run in observe-only mode against next-available runtime change.
2) Canary: enable controller to pause and auto-approve small slices (1-3% traffic) with synthetic probes enabled.
3) Progressive: expand slices (5% -> 20% -> 50%) only while all synthetic assertions pass and no tail-latency regressions observed.
4) Full: if all gates pass, complete apply.
5) Fast rollback: if any critical gate fails, automatically trigger backout steps and alert on-call.
health_checks_and_thresholds:
- Synthetic probe success rate >= 99% over 60s window per slice.
- Rolling p99 latency delta <= +20ms compared to baseline across slices.
- Error-rate increase <= 0.25% absolute.
- KV cache miss ratio within expected variance (configurable per-tenant).
- Trace-based request jitter (95->99 percentile delta) monitored and fed to decision engine.
terraform_changes:
- New module: private_runtime_rollout_v1 with inputs: target_variant, slice_selector, probe_config, rollback_policy.
- Module outputs: plan_id, expected_priming_work, preflight_checks_hash for controller.
- Make applies guarded: apply only via controller using plan_id token.
- State locking: integrate with existing backend (S3/Lock) but add controller-level lease to prevent manual concurrent applies.
- Migration: small migration script to update existing private stacks to include controller-managed rollout tags.
implementation_notes:
- Controller implemented as Kubernetes operator (Go) using controller-runtime.
- Decision engine rules encoded as Lua scripts for rapid iteration; stored in ConfigMap and versioned.
- Synthetic prober written in Rust for low overhead; image registry: registry.redwood-internal/probers:2026-02.
- Observability: emit structured events to Console under rollout.* namespace and create automatic Grafana dashboard per rollout.
- API endpoints for manual emergency rollback with reasons logged for audit.
testing_strategy:
- Unit tests for FSM decision engine.
- Integration tests: local k8s (kind) runs with simulated KV backend and load generator.
- Staging rehearsal: run against our staging VPC with production-like tenant slices.
- Chaos tests: introduce transient network partitions and KV latency spikes to validate rollback correctness.
- Run 5 full staging rollouts and record metrics before promoting to private-beta.

risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: false positives from synthetic probes cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require two independent signals (probe + trace tail-latency) to trigger critical rollback.
- Risk: Terraform API drift or operator lease collisions. Mitigation: add preflight checks and safe-fail to manual approval.
- Risk: prolonged rollback impacts sessions. Mitigation: prefer connection-preserving handoff where runtime supports it; document expected client behavior.
